audit.whatIsWrong: The chart gives six of seven stages to Warwick and Level 6 to 'Skill', while Sejuani wins 56.12% over 98 games and the entry's own prose says 'At Level 2, Arctic Assault changes everything' and 'At Level 6 your lane tilts hard in your favor'.
audit.why: The chart is the opposite of the text beside it and of the record. The packet levelChart reads Skill / Sejuani / Sejuani / Skill / Sejuani / Sejuani / Sejuani and matches the kits: Warwick's only gap-close pre-6 is Jaws of the Beast at 365 units, so Arctic Assault at 650 opens the trade from outside his range from level 2 onward.
audit.corrected: Levels 2, 3, 6, first item and 2+ items belong to Sejuani; Level 1 and Levels 4-5 are even.

audit.whatIsWrong: The first-item spike claims Sunfire Aegis or Heartsteel 'makes you genuinely unkillable to a drain bruiser'. Jaws of the Beast deals damage based on the target's maximum health.
audit.why: Stacking health is the one build direction that feeds Warwick's Q, so the entry's headline item advice makes the problem it names worse — Heartsteel in particular raises the number his percent-max-health bite deals. Grievous Wounds is the actual first-item decision here and it is absent from both layers, even though three separate parts of his kit heal: Eternal Hunger, Jaws of the Beast and Infinite Duress.
audit.corrected: Jaws of the Beast scales off your maximum health, so bulk alone reads the trade wrong. Buy Grievous Wounds on the first tank item — Eternal Hunger, Jaws of the Beast and Infinite Duress all heal him.
sources: champ-data/_kits/warwick.json (Jaws of the Beast 'damage based on their maximum health and healing for damage dealt', percentHealth flag; Eternal Hunger and Infinite Duress heal flags)

audit.whatIsWrong: Infinite Duress is a channel. Sejuani's Permafrost and Glacial Prison cancel it outright. Neither layer says so anywhere; both instead teach that R must be thrown first to 'pre-empt' the suppress.
audit.why: This is the decisive interaction of the matchup and it changes the whole ordering of the fight. As the entry is written, the Sejuani player spends Glacial Prison on the approach and then has nothing left when Warwick lands the suppress. Because the suppress is a channel, holding a stun instead means his ultimate is not something to avoid — it is a 110-second cooldown he hands you. Permafrost is on 1.5 seconds and only needs a target at full Frost, so the stun that breaks his R is one you can realistically have ready, and cancelling it mid-channel is strictly better than out-ranging it.
audit.corrected: Infinite Duress is a channel — Permafrost or Glacial Prison cancels it mid-suppress. Hold a stun for his ultimate rather than spending R to stay out of its way.
sources: champ-data/_kits/_missing-interactions.json ('Warwick's Infinite Duress (R) is a channel — your Fury of the North (P), Permafrost (E), Glacial Prison (R) cancels it outright')

audit.whatIsWrong: Primal Howl is never mentioned in either layer. It is Warwick's E: 2.5 seconds of damage reduction, then a fear that makes nearby enemies flee for 1 second, on a 15/14/13/12/11 second cooldown.
audit.why: It is the only thing in his kit that breaks a Sejuani combo mid-cast, and it does it twice over — the damage reduction blunts the Permafrost shatter and the fear walks her out of Winter's Wrath range before the second arc lands. An entry that tells the player 'one clean engage ends the trade decisively in your favor' without mentioning the 15-second button that undoes exactly that engage is setting up the failure it is trying to prevent.
audit.corrected: Primal Howl: 15/14/13/12/11s. Damage reduction for 2.5 seconds, then a 1-second fear — it blunts the shatter and walks you out of your own W.
sources: champ-data/_kits/warwick.json (Primal Howl cd 15/14/13/12/11, 'damage reduction for 2.5 seconds. At the end, or if re-activated, he howls, causing nearby enemies to flee for 1 second', hardCC flag)

audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer credits Sejuani's resistances to 'passive Permafrost resistances' in three places. Permafrost is her E stun and has no passive; the armour and MR come from Frost Armor on Fury of the North, which requires being out of combat.
audit.why: Against Warwick specifically the condition matters more than usual, because his gameplan is uninterrupted contact — Frost Armor falls off shortly after she takes damage, so the resistances the entry says will out-regenerate his drain are precisely the ones his drain removes. Attaching them to the E hides that.
audit.corrected: The resistances are Frost Armor from Fury of the North, gained out of combat and lost shortly after she takes damage — Warwick's sustained contact is what strips it.
sources: champ-data/_kits/sejuani.json (Fury of the North and Permafrost descriptions)

edits.after: Infinite Duress is a channel — Permafrost or Glacial Prison cancels it mid-suppress, so bank a stun for his R, not for the approach.

edits.after: Jaws of the Beast damages you by your own maximum health, so raw bulk feeds it — take Grievous Wounds with the first tank item instead of a second health component.

edits.before: Glacial Prison outranges Infinite Duress — throw R first to lock him in the blizzard, then walk in for Q-W-E; you have neutralized his entire win condition before it starts.
edits.after: Infinite Duress is a channel — Permafrost or Glacial Prison cancels the suppress mid-cast, so bank your stun for his R instead of spending it on the approach.

edits.after: Grievous Wounds tips the drain battle, not raw bulk: Jaws of the Beast scales off your maximum health, so tank items feed it, and Eternal Hunger triples its healing the moment he drops below 25%.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are the most neutral window: your damage doesn't spike with levels and his sustain makes short trades punishing if you don't have the full Q-W-E chain available, so only fight when all three are up. At Level 6 your lane tilts hard in your favor — Glacial Prison outranges Infinite Duress entirely, meaning you can lock him from distance before he ever has the chance to jump onto you and suppress. Land R to root him in the blizzard, then walk in for Q-W-E while he is still frozen. He cannot respond with his R because yours resolved first; once Infinite Duress is on cooldown he has no answer to your CC chain.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are the most neutral window: your damage doesn't spike with levels and his sustain makes short trades punishing without the full Q-W-E chain, so only fight when all three are up and Primal Howl is down — 15s at rank 1, and its fear walks you out of Winter's Wrath. At Level 6 the lane tilts hard your way, but not for the reason you would guess: Infinite Duress is a channel, so Permafrost or Glacial Prison cancels the suppress outright. Do not spend R staying out of his range — let him commit 110 seconds of ultimate, break it with a stun, and take the fight while he has nothing left.

edits.before: - Warwick Infinite Duress: matchup-defining — Lock-on suppress — track it before every step-up. Step up only on its downtime. - Budget Q dash for emergencies and the R for opportunities — never swap them.
edits.after: - Warwick Infinite Duress: 110/90/70s, and it is a channel — your stun cancels the suppress outright, so hold one for it. - Primal Howl: 15s at rank 1, damage reduction into a fear. - Blood Hunt: 80s at rank 1.

notes: Best find: Infinite Duress is a channel, so Permafrost or Glacial Prison cancels the suppress mid-cast. Both layers instead teach the player to spend Glacial Prison pre-emptively to out-range it, which leaves him with no answer when the suppress actually lands. Holding a stun turns Warwick's 110-second ultimate into a gift rather than a threat, and this is the single interaction the whole matchup turns on. Second: Primal Howl appears nowhere in either layer. It is 15s at rank 1, gives 2.5 seconds of damage reduction and then a 1-second fear — the only button in his kit that breaks the Sejuani combo mid-cast, and it undoes exactly the 'one clean engage' the entry promises. Third: the first-item spike says Sunfire Aegis or Heartsteel makes you 'genuinely unkillable to a drain bruiser', but Jaws of the Beast deals damage based on your maximum health, so stacking HP feeds it; Grievous Wounds is the real first-item call and anti-heal is absent from both layers even though three parts of his kit heal.
